_about: OBSERVED facts about checkpoints — what inspection returned, never what anyone declared. `roster/models/models.yaml` is the authored side; this is the found side; ClickHouse is the join.
_why_one_file: The archive kept these in SIX artifacts (tokenizer_properties.json, weights_audit.csv, cjk_coverage.csv, bos_resolution.csv, tokenizer_roundtrip.csv, model_revisions.json), each independently defining 'the set of models', and they drifted: 32 sources declared against 51 on disk, a params audit reading a 9-day-old roster and measuring two thirds of it. One file with a stamped section per pass cannot half-update.
_stamp_rule: Every section carries `measured_at` and `n`. A measurement of a checkpoint is only true of that checkpoint AS IT STOOD; an unstamped observation cannot be told from a stale one.

weights_from_files._why: A SECOND ROUTE, NOT A RESTAMP OF THE FIRST. `weights` measured 138 checkpoints on 2026-08-15 via model_info(expand=['safetensors']) and named 19 it could not reach: those repos publish .bin, so no safetensors header exists for the Hub to index and re-running that call can never help. This section measures those 19 plus 7 added to models.yaml afterwards, from file sizes. `weights` is left exactly as it stood -- restamping it would assert a freshness that did not happen -- and roster._measured_params() reads every section, taking the later measured_at on conflict.
weights_from_files.measured_by: scripts/measure_weights_from_files.py: huggingface_hub HfApi().model_info(files_metadata=True) -> sum of weight-shard `size` / bytes-per-param read from the first shard's header (safetensors JSON header or pickle *Storage token, HTTP Range, no weights downloaded); cross-checked against the transformer parameter formula on config.json. No safetensors metadata is involved, which is why it reaches the .bin repos `weights` could not.
